newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- OCT 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- OCT 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--The Turkish strategy to increase tension on divided Cyprus claims its fourth victim. Unarmed Petros Kakoulis mistakenly strays into Turkish-occupied territory and is shot by Turkish occupation troops. Turkish intention is to convince the world that the two communities cannot live together. Cyprus is determined to bring the latest issue to the UN Security Council.
--Government tries to fend off criticism of its appointment of Sunday newspaper 'To Vima' publisher Stavros Psyharis to post of governor of autonomous monastic community of Mount Athos.
--Former Yugoslav Republic of Macedonia name issue due to be resolved with triple name option by year's end, diplomatic sources say.

--Parliament to see first bills on tax exemptions, public expenditures within the next few weeks, in first steps to putting economic house in order. The government will immediately proceed with a freeze on public sector appointments and strict control on spending by state utilities and organisations (DEKO).

--Objective tax criteria at the mercy of the courts. Provisions setting tax levels for merchants and self-employed professionals on the basis of the rental of business premises to be ruled anti-constitutional.
--Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis closes down Greece's own Open University - the brainchild of former minister George Papandreou - before it opens.

--Leading New Democracy member Stephanos Manos fears split in main opposition party in forthcoming congress is stacked or if leader Miltiades Evert 'blocks developments'. Evert must not seek the leadership at the congress, he says. Failed leadership candidate George Souflias's unity proposal has room for all - including Evert.
